title: The US Must End Its Illegal Boat Strikes
author: Farrah Hassen
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/05/474a4ba0-afb8-11f0-b2a1-6f537f66f9aa.jpg-680x383.webp)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/05/15/the-
us-must-end-its-illegal-boat-strikes/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/05/474a4ba0-afb8-11f0-b2a1-6f537f66f9aa.jpg-680x383.webp)

Still from video of a boat strike posted to X by Pete Hegesth.

The U.S. military has been carrying out [extrajudicial
killings](https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/09/18/us-maritime-strikes-amount-to-
extrajudicial-killings) in the Caribbean and Pacific over the past nine months
with impunity.

On May 8, the U.S. military struck another boat in the eastern Pacific,
[killing two people and leaving one
survivor](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/us-strike-
alleged-drug-boat-eastern-pacific-kills-2-leaves-survivor-rcna344320). U.S.
Southern Command [claimed](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/9/us-
military-kills-two-people-in-new-eastern-pacific-ocean-attack) “the vessel was
transiting along known narco-trafficking routes” and “was engaged in narco-
trafficking operations.”

According to [_The Intercept_](https://theintercept.com/2025/11/17/trump-boat-
strikes-death-toll-caribbean-pacific/), there have now been 58 such boat
strikes since September that have killed at least 193 people. As with the May
8 attack, the names and nationalities of most of these victims remain unknown.

The Trump administration has accused civilian boats of transporting narcotics
to the U.S. and says its killing “narco-terrorists.” But the Pentagon has
provided no evidence for these claims or any indication that the people killed
posed an imminent threat.

International and U.S. law do not allow the use of the military to kill
civilians suspected of crimes. Boat bombing on the high seas is not a
legitimate law enforcement operation. Nor is it [curbing the flow of
drugs](https://theintercept.com/2026/05/04/trump-boat-strikes-fentanyl-
cocaine-drug-
supply/?fbclid=IwY2xjawRwVFxleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETFtbU85bWNSb05KekdEeXRyc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABHr8d7hbKlZLqTdSB2dQi_Dn6ZufITzkgPJWcnxM4p0WYNNKx0QaJ6LETaubI_aem_PeevcMu8B_GlT33L677KkQ)
into the United States, as Trump claims, or combating the root causes of drug
use.

Even if the boats  _did_ carry drugs, the appropriate response would be to
lawfully intercept and detain the suspects and afford them due process of law.

In a desperate attempt to provide legal cover for these murders, the Trump
administration is asserting that the U.S. is engaged in an “armed conflict”
with unspecified drug cartels — the same kind of broad legal authority invoked
by the George W. Bush administration in its post-9/11 “war on terror.”

But there is no armed conflict in the Caribbean or the Pacific. The people on
those boats are civilians who are not legitimate military targets. “You just
can’t call something war to give yourself war powers,”
[noted](https://apnews.com/article/trump-maduro-drugs-
venezuela-911-hegseth-3db3aafed492556bb9ca7de855c4849e) University of
Pennsylvania professor Claire Finkelstein.

Legal and human rights experts agree.

Last October, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk
[condemned](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2025/10/us-attacks-
caribbean-and-pacific-violate-international-human-rights-law-un) the boat
strikes. “None of the individuals on the targeted boats appeared to pose an
imminent threat to the lives of others or otherwise justified the use of
lethal armed force against them under international law,” Türk
[said](https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2025/10/us-attacks-caribbean-
and-pacific-violate-international-human-rights-law-un) in his October 31
statement.

Despite the unsubstantiated, fear-mongering claims pushed by the Trump
administration, investigations have shown that several of those people killed
were fishermen trying to make a living for their families. On January 20, the
U.S. [attacked](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/rare-survivors-of-pacific-boat-
strikes) the Ecuadorian fishing boat  _La Fiorella_. None of the eight
fishermen aboard have been seen since.

Survivors have also endured abuse. In two separate Pacific attacks on
Ecuadorian fishing boats in March, 36 survivors said they were “abducted and
tortured by American forces and taken by boat all the way to El Salvador
before being returned to Ecuador,” according to an investigation by [_Drop
Site News_](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/rare-survivors-of-pacific-boat-
strikes).

“They handcuffed us, put hoods over our heads and pushed us around. We were
terrified they were going to kill us,”
[recalled](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/apr/21/ecuador-
us-boat-strike-survivors) Jhonny Sebastián Palacios, one of the survivors, in
an interview with _The Guardian_.

The U.S. must immediately end these boat strikes and take accountability for
the harms caused to the victims and their families. And Congress must do its
job of conducting oversight to ensure transparent and independent
investigations of these strikes.

The use of unlawful force will become more normalized at home and abroad
unless the Trump administration is held accountable for these illegal killings
and its blatant abuse of power.

When federal immigration agents [killed American
citizens](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/ice-shootings-list-border-
patrol-trump-immigration-operations-rcna254202) earlier this year, we saw all
too clearly the risks of letting the government shoot people and [call them
“terrorists.”](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/noem-doesnt-retract-
calling-us-citizens-killed-immigration-agents-dome-rcna261499) It leaves all
of us less secure, undermines the rule of law, and can’t be allowed to become
routine.
